claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.1, annual return 4%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.15 to 1.15 (change +0.00).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.15 to 1.15. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.05 (as submitted, 3 bps: 1.15); it breaks even at 81.6 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.15 against 1.15 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 0.09 against 1.15 in research, a gap of +1.06.
The best year gives 51% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give 160%; Sharpe is 2.57 in calm and -2.56 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 246 distinct specs; the best of 246 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 1.41, so the claimed 1.10 becomes -0.31 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 26%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.19 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.04, 95th percentile 0.84).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.15 to as low as -0.17 (as low as -0.17 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (11 days) give 45% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 53% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
